detail: 3 PR review comments drafted; awaiting go-ahead to post
text:
out. Traced it through `@lhci/cli`'s settings cleanup and lighthouse's own runner, then ran the exact same shape locally with a placeholder secret to check what actually happens: the value lands in plaintext in `configSettings.extraHeaders` on both the generated LHR JSON and the HTML report. Those get uploaded as a 30-day GitHub Actions artifact by the existing "Upload Lighthouse results" step, and the same report goes to the external LHCI server too, since that upload path is already wired up. So the header that gates access to SIT ends up sitting somewhere with a wider audience than whoever can read the GitHub secret itself.
>
> Worth adding regardless: `.lighthouseci/` isn't in `.gitignore`, so running this locally with the var set could also commit the secret straight into git history.
>
> Is there room to scope this down, either with a rotatable/short-lived value instead of a static bypass secret, or by stripping `configSettings` before anything gets persisted, or is the SIT gate secret already treated as low-enough stakes that this is fine as is? Not blocking, just didn't want it to slide through unnoticed.

---

**Inline — `.github/workflows/digital-sit.yml`, line 43** (the `find` check)

> This check is narrower than what the `p0` project actually collects. `playwright.config.js`'s `p0` project doesn't override `testDir`, so `testMatch: ['**/*.p0.spec.{js,ts}']` picks up specs anywhere under `e2e/`, not just `e2e/tests/zimm` (the `a11y-*` projects do scope their own `testDir`, so there's precedent either way). Confirmed by dropping a real `.p0.spec.ts` file outside `e2e/tests/zimm/` and checking `playwright test --project=p0 --list` picks it up while this `find` doesn't.
>
> Harmless today since every spec lives under `e2e/tests/zimm/` anyway, but the failure direction is the bad one: a real P0 spec added elsewhere would run for real while this still claims zero coverage, which could make a working gate look fake. One-line fix either way, scope the `find` to match `testDir`, or drop the `e2e/tests/zimm` restriction to match what `p0` actually runs.

---

**General PR comment**

> Confirmed both fixes this PR names do what they say. The P0 soft-pass and warning annotation fire correctly. Lighthouse no longer hits `CHROME_INTERSTITIAL_ERROR` and genuinely reaches SIT now, confirmed against the actual run.
>
> Left two comments below: one on the new Lighthouse header forwarding (a real question about where that secret ends up, not blocking), and one on the P0 warning check's scope (small, one-line fix).
>
> One thing worth talking through rather than fixing in this diff. After this merges, `lighthouse-ci` still fails on this PR's own run, now for real reasons: performance at 0.41 against the required 0.8, best practices at 0.83 against 0.9, plus a batch of PWA-installability, CSP and console-error findings. Nothing in this diff could move any of that, and I don't think it should try to. But it does mean release/v0.1.0's SIT Gate stays red after this merges, just for a legitimate reason instead of an infra one.
>
> Two things follow from that worth naming. First, `deploy-sit.yml` only redeploys SIT when the whole SIT Gate passes, so until the performance work happens, that path won't fire again. The `push:sit` bootstrap in the description might end up being the only fresh SIT content for a while rather than a one-off unblock. Second, you already built a soft-pass-plus-warning pattern for exactly this shape of problem on the P0 side: real gap, early-stage app, gate that would otherwise block every release branch. Curious why Lighthouse didn't get the same treatment. Is that deliberate (performance debt is worse to let slide silently than test debt, so it should stay a hard block now that it's finally measurable), or worth giving the same provisional treatment until there's a real perf push, so release/v0.1.0 isn't stuck?

---

Ready to post all three on your go — say so and I'll push them via `gh pr comment`/`gh pr review`.

text: Glad it landed well. One thing worth flagging before we close this out: CodeRabbit's automated review **never fires on any PR targeting `release/**`** — it only reviews PRs against the default branch. So going forward, the only CodeRabbit coverage on a release-targeted PR is whatever the author ran locally via `cr review --light --base main`; there's nothing to "respond to threads on" from the bot side. Saved that plus the PR #75 findings to memory for next time.
